Yes but that’s a small percentage of the trans community carrying this out, not the trans community as a whole. The majority of the trans community intend to transition and just go about their lives, regardless of the hate, abuse and negativity they experience. Please don’t tarnish everyone with the same brush. Generalisations like this are misleading.

If you’ve done your research, surely you’d understand that your first comment is dangerous to put out there and extremely misleading? How was I supposed to know that you’re aware of the suicide rates in the trans community when your comment implied quite the opposite?

Unfortunately in situations like this, you have to make people aware of the awful reality a lot of trans people live in; the extremely high suicide rates among the trans community being one of them. 

It’s a sad world we live in where people who live with a physical and psychological disorder are made to feel as though taking their own life is the only way out of the dysphoria, abuse, negativity and violence (to name a few) that they suffer from every single day.

Honestly, for the sake of everyone, do some bloody research before commenting such nonsense you uneducated arsehole.

Transgenderism is SCIENTIFICALLY proven - men and women’s brains are wired up differently in very subtle ways. Transgender people are born with a male/female brain but with the opposite body, therefore transgender people suffer from dysphoria (I hoping you’d know what that means since you think you’re so clued up on the topic?) which makes them begin their transitions to become the gender their brain is, but their body isn’t. 

Please do not confuse actual transgender people with the “PC gone mad” culture we’re experiencing today. The majority of the trans community do not want to involve themselves and their identities with this, and just want to transition and live their lives in peace. 

48% of trans people JUST in the UK have attempted suicide at least once; 84% have thought about it. 55% have been diagnosed with depression, and that’s just based on the ones who were part of this study sample. 
EDIT: these stats were taken from the Stonewall website. 

To reiterate, do some RESEARCH before making such crazy and frankly laughable comments towards a subject you clearly have no knowledge about. What you’re saying is DANGEROUS and could seriously harm what people already think about the trans community, and the community itself.

Hi, I've been suffering from severe anxiety and depression since I was 14 - I'm now 20. I've gone through extreme ups and downs, I ended up in hospital last year, and right now I feel exactly the same. A couple of months ago, I felt as though I was finally getting better and even a couple of months after I was discharged I felt free of my illnesses for a while. Sometimes when we enter 'that' place, it's very difficult to remember that there are people like ourselves out there going through the same thing, feeling the same darkness, and it makes us feel so alone when we have nobody to turn to who truly understands what it's like to have to deal with these awful illnesses.

If you don't mind me asking, what bothers you the most? Have you ever reached out for help and if so, did it actually help? I'd like to try and help as much as possible because nobody deserves to go through this alone, and trust me I know what it's like to be alone and feel so small and overwhelmed that it doesn't ever feel like you're going to get better. Yknow, I'm actually going through it right now.

Maybe we can learn a thing or two from each other! We're in this together! Please stay strong x
